elements.text: 4.2 likely exposed a persistent ranking problem
ROOK DISPATCH  /  Leadership briefing
Acceptance fell 12.6 percentage points after release
Shorter response window
90 to 60 seconds. Missed offers rose from 2.3% to 18.0%.
Persistent score penalties
Timeouts lower future ranking. Scores recover only when responders accept more work.
Strongest explanation: a release change interacting with an existing design weakness

elements.text: Timeout penalties create a cycle of fewer opportunities
ROOK DISPATCH  /  Leadership briefing
Shorter window
More responders can miss an offer before answering
Miss counts as refusal
Each non-acceptance subtracts 0.12 from the score
Lower score, lower rank
Another responder may accept before the offer reaches them
Limited route to recovery
Only an acceptance raises the score. Time alone does nothing
The 4.2 proximity change can also redistribute offers. Its separate impact remains unmeasured.

notes.text:
Source: 00-rook/code/dispatch-routing/config.py, offer.py, history.py and routing.py. Supplied course code contains stubbed availability/device functions. Verified scoring behavior locally without changing files.
Mechanism reproduction: neutral acceptance score 0.5, five consecutive non-acceptances subtract 0.12 each and clamp at zero. No decay or elapsed-time recovery exists. Ranking includes acceptance score with weight 0.25. Dispatch stops at the first acceptance. Mechanism confirmed in supplied code, production attribution inferred.

elements.text: The evidence supports action, with clear limits
ROOK DISPATCH  /  Leadership briefing
Confirmed in the sources

4.2 shortened the window

Code penalizes misses and refusals equally

Scores have no recovery with time
Still requires validation

Contribution of each release change

Historical scores and candidate availability

Delivery latency and prior-year seasonality
Release-related regression is the leading diagnosis. Exact attribution requires replay and instrumentation.

elements.text: A targeted fix addresses the trigger and lasting harm
ROOK DISPATCH  /  Leadership briefing
Recovery release
Restore the 90-second window and remove ranking penalties for missed offers
Affected responders
Validate historical timeout penalties, then correct scores where evidence supports it
Durable scoring
Design gradual recovery toward neutral and validate it before a later release
Proximity weights
Keep current weights during initial recovery. Evaluate their impact separately
Tradeoff: a longer window may slow assignment. Measure that cost during rollout.

notes.text:
Source: 00-rook/code/dispatch-routing/config.py, offer.py, history.py and routing.py. Supplied course code contains stubbed availability/device functions. Verified scoring behavior locally without changing files.
Recommendations are proposals, not implemented or validated production changes. Leadership must approve recovery rules and tradeoffs. Score correction depends on recoverable history and should not indiscriminately reset responders.
